summary_of_work: Read in full the released Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 tournament state machine: prt/contracts/src/tournament/Tournament.sol, libs/Match.sol, Clock.sol, MatchClocks.sol, Time.sol, Commitment.sol, Bond.sol, Gas.sol, factories/MultiLevelTournamentFactory.sol, arbitration-config (ArbitrationConstants, ClockBudgets, CanonicalTournamentParametersProvider), script/Deployment.s.sol clock policy, state-transition/CartesiStateTransition.sol (counter/form map only), cartesi-rollups/contracts/src/DaveConsensus.sol, plus the manual's PRT sections (doc/README.md 10395-11330) and the referee model doc/recipes/prt.lua lines 100-880. Derived and checked these invariants by reasoning over every mutator (joinTournament, advanceMatch, sealLeafMatch, winLeafMatch, sealInnerMatchAndCreateInnerTournament, winInnerTournament, eliminateInnerTournament, winMatchByTimeout, eliminateMatchByTimeout, tryRecoveringBond) and views (innerResult, tournamentStanding): (I1) a commitment root joins at most once per tournament (clock requireUninitialized; a positive initial allowance is guaranteed by the !closed gate), is either dangling or in at most one live match, and at most one commitment is dangling; (I2) the bisection invariant otherParent != join(leftNode,rightNode) holds from Match.create through every advance, so the seal always finds two distinct divergent leaves, finalStateOne != finalStateTwo, and both claims agree on every leaf left of the divergence; the agreed state is authenticated at height 0 of the full tree in the revealing commitment (except leaf 0, the confirmed R7-MANTOURN-1); seal parity (height odd -> one reveals last) matches clock parity; (I3) leaf/counter geometry: root leaf p = state after counter (p+1)*2^38-1, child startCycle = d*2^38 and initialHash = root leaf d-1, child last leaf = root leaf d, winLeafMatch verifies counter startCycle+d from leaf d-1, consistent with CartesiStateTransition's 'counter indexes the output leaf'; (I4) clocks: every write keeps a positive allowance (pauseAfterResponseAt reverts at/after the deadline, pauseWinnerAt is gated by the classifier's strict remaining > deferred, childReturnAllowance >= min(carried, envelope) > 0, innerResult's deductPaused is gated by non-expiry), no clock exceeds the pair envelope <= maxAllowance, the only increase is the documented refill on child return; the bisection/leaf-race/sealed-inner clock shapes are preserved by every transition, so no reachable assert (Panic) exists on a progress path; (I5) proof, single-winner timeout and double elimination are disjoint at each instant (inclusive deadlines on both sides), sealed inner matches classify NONE, and a sealed inner match is deletable only through its recorded child (matchIdFromInnerTournaments set only at seal, cleared on both deletion paths; factory clones use CREATE so orphans cannot collide); (I6) the root result is immutable once closed with matchCount 0 (every mutator requires !finished and matchCount cannot go 0 -> positive after closure), the root winner's finalState is the last leaf proven at join, an inner WINNER maps to the parent commitment through its final state only, and a root cannot finish while any linked child is live (so DaveConsensus.provideMerkleRootOfInput's use of the current epoch's bounds cannot reach an older epoch's leaf match); (I7) acting for another commitment (join of its root, advance, seal, timeout win, leaf proof, propagation) is deterministic given its tree and never charges it more than its own latency would; front-running a join only moves the claimer/bond payout; (I8) refunds are progress-gated, metered on proofs.length that the STF fixes, capped per action and by balance, paid after all state effects while the instance lock is held; per-join match work reserves cover one match's actions; terminal payment preserves state on a failed callback. I found no input sequence that breaks any of them. Differences from the manual's referee model that I saw (asynchronous pairing, propagation transaction and winner expiry, proof only before the earlier leaf deadline, Dave's timeout win between two provably wrong leaf claims) are listed as simplifications in doc/README.md ('The model simplifies the PRT contracts in a few ways') or already reported (R1-A2-2, R2-DFCLAIM-1, R7-MANTOURN-1, R8-GOALTIMEOUT-2). Considered and not reported: excess join value is pooled (documented in dispute-game.md and prt-refund-accounting.md); each child stays open until start + max(r1, r2), about one week on mainnet, even when both sides have resolved, which multiplies settlement delay per sealed match (liveness only, mirrored by the referee model, and covered by Dave's documented delay non-claims; no rule of THREAT_MODEL.md is violated); the 47,700-gas winner-payment callback can make a bond permanently unrecoverable for a contract claimer whose receive costs more (economic, documented bounded callbacks). No experiment was run: building a forge project for new tests needs a ~15 minute via-IR compile of a copy of the harness build, which I judged not worthwhile without a candidate; Dave's own released suites (427/447, failures limited to step-fixture roots) were taken from the harness record.
not_covered: No forge or anvil experiment was run for this angle; all invariants were checked by reading the released sources (Tournament, Match, Clock, MatchClocks, Time, Commitment, Bond, Gas, factory, provider, DaveConsensus).

Quantitative A7 sizing (whether G = 5 min, T = 120 min and C = 1 week cover the honest root join after EpochSealed, the child build of a worst-case 2^38-leaf uarch claim, and leaf-proof generation) was not re-derived; it is covered by R1-A7-1 and R8-GOALTIMEOUT-1/2.
Gas: actual gas of every refundable action against Gas.sol allocations (and the EIP-7623 calldata floor against WIN_LEAF_MATCH's 16 gas/byte metering) was not measured.

Economic griefing of the honest signer through front-run reverted transactions and refund caps when basefee exceeds WORK_PRICE_CAP (50 gwei) was not quantified; it is outside the threat model's goal unless it starves the honest of bond capital.
DaveConsensus staging/acceptance, sentries, foreclosure and output validation (A5 area) were read only where they consume tournamentStanding.
The referee model in doc/recipes/prt.lua was read only for its tournament state machine (lines 100-880); the game transport, clock server and stored-player paths were not.
CartesiStateTransition and the step libraries were read only for the counter-to-form map, not for verifier soundness.
docs/prt-delay-bound.md and docs/dimensioning.md were not read; the delay bounds they claim were not checked. docs/reviews was deliberately not read (earlier review material).
